beats.title: Voltaire's Zadig
beats.description: A philosophical tale shows its hero deducing the look of a missing animal from tracks alone, an early model of detective logic.
beats.note: First printed 1747 as Memnon; the Zadig title came in 1748

beats.title: Godwin's Caleb Williams
beats.description: A servant uncovers his master's murder secret and is hounded across the country in William Godwin's pioneering crime novel.

beats.title: Poe's Murders in the Rue Morgue
beats.description: Auguste Dupin solves a gruesome double killing in a locked room, launching the detective story as a form.

beats.title: Poe's Mystery of Marie Roget
beats.description: Dupin untangles the death of a Parisian shop girl purely from newspaper reports, in the first story based on a real case.

beats.title: Bleak House Brings Inspector Bucket
beats.description: Dickens serialises a sprawling novel in which a shrewd police detective investigates a lawyer's murder.

beats.title: The Woman in White Begins Its Run
beats.description: Wilkie Collins serialises a tale of switched identities, a sinister count and an amateur sleuth, a sensation of the day.

beats.title: Gaboriau's Lerouge Case Debuts
beats.description: A French novelist's tale of a murdered widow introduces a police detective and sets the pattern for the detective novel.
beats.note: Book form 1866; serialised in Le Pays shortly before

beats.title: Collins Publishes The Moonstone
beats.description: A stolen Indian diamond, a bumbling household and the dogged Sergeant Cuff form the first great English detective novel.

beats.title: The Leavenworth Case Hooks America
beats.description: Anna Katharine Green's novel of a rich man shot in his library becomes a bestseller and a model for American detective fiction.

beats.title: Sherlock Holmes Debuts
beats.description: A Study in Scarlet introduces a consulting detective and his doctor friend to the reading public.

beats.title: Holmes Conquers the Strand Magazine
beats.description: A monthly short story about a King and a photograph begins a run of tales that turn the detective into a sensation.

beats.title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
beats.description: A spectral dog haunts a moorland estate, and Holmes is called back to confront the legend of a cursed family.

beats.title: The Mystery of the Yellow Room
beats.description: A French novel poses the classic locked-room puzzle: a woman attacked in a chamber no one could have entered or left.

beats.title: Father Brown Debuts
beats.description: G. K. Chesterton's unassuming priest solves a crime with insight into human nature in The Blue Cross.

beats.title: Trent's Last Case
beats.description: E. C. Bentley's novel gives a murdered financier, a charming amateur sleuth and a twist ending that stunned readers.

beats.title: Poirot Debuts at Styles
beats.description: A Belgian refugee with an egg-shaped head and little grey cells solves a poisoning at an Essex country house.
beats.note: US first edition October 1920; UK edition January 1921

beats.title: Lord Peter Wimsey Debuts
beats.description: Dorothy L. Sayers introduces an aristocratic amateur detective who finds a corpse in a bathtub wearing only a pince-nez.

beats.title: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd
beats.description: Christie's notorious novel springs a narrator twist that divided critics and changed what a mystery could do.

beats.title: Hammett's The Maltese Falcon
beats.description: Sam Spade hunts a jewelled bird statuette among liars and killers in the defining hard-boiled detective novel.
beats.note: Book form 1930; Black Mask serial began 1929

beats.title: Murder on the Orient Express
beats.description: A snowbound luxury train, a stabbed American tycoon and a carriage full of suspects confront Poirot.

beats.title: The Big Sleep Introduces Marlowe
beats.description: Raymond Chandler sends a wisecracking private eye into a Los Angeles blackmail case among a wealthy family.

beats.title: Mike Hammer Debuts in I, the Jury
beats.description: Mickey Spillane's violent private eye avenges the murder of a friend in a bestseller of brutal, pulpy crime fiction.

beats.title: Lew Archer Debuts
beats.description: Ross Macdonald's California private eye takes on a missing-millionaire case in the first of a long, psychologically deep series.
beats.note: The Moving Target, 1949, under the name John Macdonald

beats.title: Tom Ripley Debuts
beats.description: Patricia Highsmith's charming con man murders his way into a rich man's life in a chilling crime novel set in Italy.

beats.title: Dalgliesh Debuts in Cover Her Face
beats.description: P. D. James introduces a poetry-writing police detective investigating a poisoning at a manor house.

beats.title: Inspector Wexford Debuts
beats.description: Ruth Rendell's calm country policeman first appears in From Doon with Death, a tale of an obsessive killer.

beats.title: Inspector Morse Debuts
beats.description: Colin Dexter's cerebral, opera-loving Oxford detective appears in Last Bus to Woodstock.

beats.title: The Name of the Rose
beats.description: A medieval friar investigates a string of deaths in a remote abbey in Umberto Eco's erudite, bestselling mystery.

beats.title: A Is for Alibi Starts the Alphabet
beats.description: Sue Grafton's Kinsey Millhone, a Californian private investigator, opens an alphabet-titled series of mysteries.

beats.title: Rebus Debuts in Knots and Crosses
beats.description: Ian Rankin's hard-drinking Edinburgh detective first appears in a case of a serial killer taunting the police.

beats.title: Scarpetta Debuts in Postmortem
beats.description: Patricia Cornwell's Virginia medical examiner hunts a serial strangler, launching the forensic crime novel boom.

beats.title: Donna Tartt's The Secret History
beats.description: A group of classics students at a New England college kill a friend, with the reader told the crime on the first page.

beats.title: The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency
beats.description: Alexander McCall Smith's gentle Botswana mysteries follow Precious Ramotswe, her country's first female private detective.

beats.title: Dan Brown's The Da Vinci Code
beats.description: A symbologist races across Europe to decode a murder at a museum and a secret guarded for centuries.

beats.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
beats.description: A disgraced journalist and a hacker investigate a decades-old disappearance in Stieg Larsson's Swedish crime sensation.

beats.title: Gillian Flynn's Gone Girl
beats.description: A wife vanishes on her wedding anniversary and her husband becomes the prime suspect in a twisty psychological thriller.

beats.title: Cormoran Strike Debuts
beats.description: J. K. Rowling, writing as Robert Galbraith, introduces a one-legged war veteran turned private eye in The Cuckoo's Calling.

beats.title: The Thursday Murder Club
beats.description: Richard Osman's debut follows four retirees who meet weekly to solve cold cases and stumble onto a fresh killing.
